from O(slog(N)) measurements one can recover an image up to its s-best term approximation of its gradient, and that this factor of log(N) can be removed by increasing the number of measurements by a logarithmic factor.

from a small number of linear measurements of a natural image, the image can be reconstructed with a small error, where the number of measurements is logarithmic in the image size, the error is proportional to the best s-term gradient approximation of the image, and the constant of proportionality can be removed with a small increase in the number of measurements.
total variation minimization can reconstruct images from a number of linear measurements that is proportional to the image sparsity, and that this number of measurements is optimal up to a logarithm.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the recovery of a function from noisy measurements of its gradient using total variation minimisation.
the recovery of images from undersampled noisy data.
the problem of reconstructing images from incomplete and noisy measurements.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the number of samples required for image recovery from noisy measurements is O(s log(N)), where N denotes the image size, s denotes the number of non-zero Fourier coefficients in the image, and the logarithmic factor can be removed.
, given a function f, we can reconstruct the gradient of the best s-term polynomial approximation of f to within an error of O(log(N)/s) using O(s log(N)/s) nonadaptive measurements.

from O(s) nonadaptive linear measurements an image can be recovered to within the best 2s-term approximation of its second derivative up to a logarithm factor, which can be removed by slightly more measurements.

The main takeaway from our work is that

total variation minimization can recover a signal with a small number of measurements, even in the presence of noise, provided that the measurements are suitably incoherence with respect to the signal’s gradient.
total variation minimization can be used to reconstruct an image from a small number of measurements without requiring any prior knowledge of the image or the noise.
total variation minimization is a near-optimal algorithm for image reconstruction from a surprisingly small number of linear measurements.
